journey.change: The team needed a way to swap and test multiple AI models without locking into one provider or rebuilding infrastructure.
journey.solution: Next.js on Vercel, plus AI SDK, AI Gateway, and Fluid compute, let SERHANT. iterate quickly, unify model access, and scale smoothly.

outcome: Feature development cut from months to a week

journey.before: Shopify’s Hydrogen storefront framework needed custom glue code and slower feature delivery.
journey.goal: Rebuild Hydrogen into an open, runtime-agnostic foundation for faster storefront development.
journey.change: The team needed a way to make Hydrogen work cleanly across frameworks without extra glue code.
journey.solution: Shopify partnered with Vercel to rebuild Hydrogen, and the story shows Next.js as one supported framework.

outcome: 15,000+ custom domains served from one codebase

journey.before: Super had been built on Gatsby and Netlify before switching to a Next.js + Vercel setup.
journey.goal: They wanted to run a fast, easy-to-manage multi-tenant website platform with custom domains at scale.
journey.change: They needed a way to manage thousands of domains and keep content updates fast without redeploying.
journey.solution: Next.js on Vercel, plus Domains API, ISR, Edge Middleware, and Preview Deployments, removed the scaling and deployment blockers.

outcome: Faster, more reliable ecommerce with improved performance and UX

journey.before: Tekla was on Gatsby Cloud and WooCommerce, struggling with buggy, slow builds and limited flexibility.
journey.goal: They wanted a scalable, high-performance ecommerce foundation that could handle traffic and support personalized experiences.
journey.change: Their existing stack needed to become faster, more reliable, and more composable without sacrificing speed at scale.
journey.solution: Agilo moved Tekla to Vercel and Medusa, and the team is planning Next.js adoption with Vercel analytics and observability to improve performance further.

outcome: Build times dropped from a full day to 2 minutes

journey.before: Tray.ai was running on an older Next.js version with Serverless, large builds, and a rigid deploy pipeline that made previews slow and releases fragile.
journey.goal: They wanted to modernize the marketing site, simplify the architecture, and unify content and form management in one system.
journey.change: Siloed repos, slow builds, and previewing changes only through full deploys were blocking faster iteration and reliable rollouts.
journey.solution: Roboto Studio rebuilt the site on Next.js in a Turborepo on Vercel, using Preview Deployments, Vercel Functions, Web Analytics, Speed Insights, and Firewall to speed delivery and improve visibility.

outcome: 2-minute builds and 3-second page loads at global scale

journey.before: Both startups were scaling fast without a dedicated DevOps team, and Leonardo.AI was bogged down by slow builds, slow pages, and infrastructure overhead.
journey.goal: They needed to keep shipping AI products globally while staying lean and avoiding a DevOps hire.
journey.change: Their infrastructure had to scale automatically without manual provisioning, babysitting, or on-call-heavy ops work.
journey.solution: Vercel enabled automated provisioning and global scale, with v0 and the Vercel REST API for deployment workflows, plus Vercel Observability and Fluid compute for performance visibility and efficient execution.

outcome: Faster AI app development with real-time brand-aware chat

journey.before: Sitecore wanted to build an AI brand assistant, but existing AI SDKs centered on backend capabilities rather than frontend experience.
journey.goal: They aimed to create Sitecore Stream, a dynamic assistant that helps marketers interact with brand assets and generate content in real time.
journey.change: The team needed a way to combine AI performance with a polished conversational UI and real-time streaming across backend and frontend.
journey.solution: They used the AI SDK with Next.js to connect Python/Azure backends to an interactive, streamed frontend experience.

outcome: Faster MCP server deployment with seamless scaling and transport support

journey.before: Vapi’s MCP server was previously deployed with only Server-Sent Events (SSE) transport.
journey.goal: They wanted to rebuild and scale their MCP server so agents could use Vapi’s endpoints and workflows more seamlessly.
journey.change: They needed a simpler way to deploy an MCP server that supported both SSE and Streamable HTTP while reducing infrastructure overhead.
journey.solution: Vapi rebuilt on Vercel using the MCP adapter, then used Fluid compute, Observability, Firewall, and a Next.js MCP template to ship and operate the server.

outcome: 60% increase in site traffic after migration

journey.before: L’Officiel ran a monolithic Ruby on Rails stack on a physical server, which was hard to manage, unreliable, and costly to maintain across 30 web properties.
journey.goal: They wanted better SEO visibility and less infrastructure overhead while supporting a lean team managing a global media network.
journey.change: The existing stack struggled with downtime, traffic spikes, and manual domain/SSL maintenance, making growth and operations difficult.
journey.solution: They migrated to Vercel and Next.js, using Next.js for SEO-friendly performance and ISR for fast updates on a large article catalog.

outcome: 10x faster development and 25x lower costs

journey.before: They managed separate client servers and WordPress monoliths, with repetitive infrastructure and slow onboarding.
journey.goal: They needed a scalable way to run many country- and brand-specific sites from one workflow.
journey.change: The blocker was fragmented code and data across clients, which made new sites slow and costly to launch.
journey.solution: They combined Next.js, Turborepo, Preview Deployments, and Vercel's edge/serverless platform with DatoCMS to centralize code, content, and deployment.
